Bangalore is the capital of Karnataka states and known as Silicon Valley of India” and also known as “The Garden City of India“. This is the 3rd most populated city of India. The foundation for Bangalore was laid Kempe Gowda, feudal ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire. It was also ruled by Maharajas of Mysore, Haider Ali and the British. There are several interesting tourist places to explore in Bangalore such as Bangalore palace, famous Temples and beautiful gardens.

Mysore is also very interesting place and also known as the historical capital of Karnataka. There are lots of thing to explore here as the grand palaces, ancient temples, rich flora and fauna and a tranquil environment. Our Bangalore Mysore packages could be a stress-free quick trip to this historical city of Mysore and modern city Bangalore. You can also explore the important things in Mysore such as silk sarees, sculptures, sandal wood products, Mysore betel leaves, Coffee powder, Mysore rosewood inlay artifacts, Mysore painting, Channapatna toys, and incense sticks.

itinerary.title: Arrive Bangalore - Local City Tour
paragraphs: Morning arrive in Bangalore. Meeting and assistance on arrival and transfer to Hotel with WTI Tours & Travels Representative.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.title: Bangalore - Mysore (3.5 Hrs drive)
paragraphs: After breakfast we drive to Mysore. En-route, we will be visiting the Ranganathaswamy Temple and Srirangapatnam, which is the capital of Tipu Sultan, and Channapatna Toys Center.
Later continue drive to Mysore. On arrival transfer to hotel and check in. Stay overnight at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.title: Mysore Sightseeing
paragraphs: Morning after breakfast we will proceed to full day sightseeing of Mysore city visiting Mysore Palace – a three storied structure in the Indo-Saracenic style built between 1897-1912. The walled palace complex houses the Residential Museum (incorporating some of the Palace’s living quarters), temples and shrines including the Shwetha Varahaswamy temple.
Also visit Sri Jayachamarajendra Art Gallery, Krishnarajasagar Dam, St. Philomena’s Church, KRS Brindavan Gardens.
We will also visit the temple at Chamundi Hills, devoted to Goddess Chamundeshwari. She is the deity of the royal family of Mysore.

In the afternoon excursion to Somanathpur Temple. Somnathpur is a small village on the banks of the river Cauvery that was founded by the commander of the Hoyasala army, Somnath. The village is famous for its splendid and grand Keshava temple that has been built in the Hoyasala style. The temple is famous for its elaborate and intricate sculpturing. The temple is enclosed in a walled courtyard that has a gate and a porch.

paragraphs: Today we will leave for Jaipur “Pink City” of Rajasthan.

Maharaja Jai Singh, who was only 11 years old, came into power after the demise of his father Maharaja Bishan Singh. Enjoy Elephant ride to reach the Fort situated on the hill, an overwhelming experience.

The center of the palace is a seven-storied building called Chandra Palace, with fine views over the gardens & the city. Further we visit Jantar Mantar (Solar Observatory), an astronomical treasure house, with solar devices that give accurate predictions till date. itinerary.title: Jaipur - Agra (4.5 Hrs Drive)
paragraphs: Today we will proceed for Agra, beautifully situated on the banks of river Yamuna. It achieved prominence as the capital of the Mughal Emperors from the year 1526 to 1628, remains major tourist destination because of its many splendid Mughal-era monuments, most notably the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort & Fatehpur Sikri, all three are UNESCO World Heritage sites.
On the way to Agra we can see Abhaneri Step Well and Fatehpur Sikri Fort.
Overnight stay at Hotel in Agra.

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.title: Agra - Delhi (3.5 Hrs Drive)
paragraphs: Sunrise we will visit to Taj Mahal, a symbol of eternal love, which stands on the banks of River Yamuna. It was built by the 5th Mughal emperor, Shah Jehan in the memory of his wife, Mumtaz Mahal. It was completed in 22 years with the orders of Shah Jahan and it was dedicated to Mumtaz Mahal (Arjumand Bano Begum), the wife of Shah. 20.000 workers labored and 32 crore rupees were spent during the construction of the monument and it was built according to Islamic architecture.
Back to hotel for the Breakfast.

Later check out around 11:00 AM and later we will visit Agra Fort, is a UNESCO World Heritage site located in Agra, India. The fort is also known as Lal Qila, Fort Rouge and Red Fort of Agra. The fort can be more accurately described as a walled palatial city. It was constructed by the third Mughal emperor Akbar on the remains of an ancient site known as Badalgarh. Some of the exquisite structures that deserve a mention are: Sheesh Mahal, the Diwan-i-Am, Diwan-i-Khas, the Anguri Bagh, Khas Mahal, Mina Masjid, Nagina Masjid and Musamman Burj – A large, octagonal tower with a balcony facing the Taj Mahal.
In the afternoon we drive back to Delhi and transfer to Airport to board flight for your onward destination.

intro: Our Overnight Agra Trip from Delhi is specially prepare for the traveler who has very short time in India and who wish to see the iconic monument “The Taj Mahal”.

Taj Mahal is the jewel of Muslim art in India and one of the universally admired masterpieces of the world’s heritage. The Taj Mahal is also one of the world’s most iconic monuments. Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal in memory of his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal. She was died in 1631 while giving birth to their 14th child. Mumtaz Mahal means ‘Jewel of the Palace’, or ‘Chosen One of the Palace. The Taj Mahal took approx 20 years and approximately 20,000 workers to complete. It is located on the bank of the Yamuna River in Agra, India. In front of the Taj Mahal, there is a beautiful vast Mughal garden and a fountain, which makes an ornament of the Taj Mahal. Taj Mahal Tour in India is a most popular tour in the world.

Taj Mahal is one of the 7th wonders of the world because; it is one of the most splendid masterpieces of architecture in the world. In the year 1983 it was listed in UNESCO world heritage site. Taj Mahal universally admired a masterpieces of the world’s heritage. We can arrange a Day Trip to Agra from Delhi. Taj Mahal Trip is also a part of our world famous Golden Triangle Tour Includes Delhi, Agra and Jaipur.

The best time to experience the mesmerizing beauty of Taj in sunrise time. Sunrise is by far the best time to visit the Taj Mahal. Not just because the early morning light turns the dome of the temple a soft, golden colour, but because this is the time when there are the least amount of tourists and if you get in early enough, you might even get some perfect portraits with no people in them.
overview: Agra is a city where the prefect romantic allure can be found. The land to the Taj Mahal, the Symbol of Love and one of the Seven Wonders of the World, makes the air of Agra full of love and romance. While the Legacy of Mughal Empire just didn’t gave Taj Mahal to this romantic land but many other mesmerizing attractions worth exploring as well

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.title: Delhi - Agra (3.5 Hrs Drive)
paragraphs: Today we will pick you from Delhi airport or your hotel in Delhi and leave for Agra. Upon arrival transfer to hotel and check in.

Afternoon we will see the Agra Fort, Agra Fort, is a UNESCO World Heritage site located in Agra, India. The fort is also known as Lal Qila, Fort Rouge and Red Fort of Agra. It is about 2.5 km northwest of its much more famous sister monument, the Taj Mahal. The fort can be more accurately described as a walled palatial city. It was constructed by the third Mughal emperor Akbar on the remains of an ancient site known as Badalgarh. Some of the exquisite structures that deserve a mention are: Sheesh Mahal, the Diwan-i-Am, Diwan-i-Khas, the Anguri Bagh, Khas Mahal, Mina Masjid, Nagina Masjid and Musamman Burj – A large, octagonal tower with a balcony facing the Taj Mahal.
Stay overnight at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.title: Agra Sightseeing - Delhi
paragraphs: Today we will see the Taj Mahal at Sunrise. Taj Mahal, an ultimate zenith of art and an enshrined romantic symbol which stands on the banks of River Yamuna. It was built by the 5th Mughal emperor, Shah Jehan in the memory of his wife, Mumtaz Mahal. It was completed in 22 years with the orders of Shah Jahan and it was dedicated to Mumtaz Mahal (Arjumand Bano Begum), the wife of Shah. The monument appears as a poem in white marble. It took 22 years to get built by 20,000 skilled artisans who laid the white marble structure with precious and semi precious stones and it was built according to Islamic architecture.
Back to Hotel for the Breakfast.

After breakfast we will see Tomb of I’timād-ud-Daulah (Baby Taj), is a Mughal mausoleum in the city of Agra. Often described as a ”jewel box”, sometimes called the ”Baby Tāj”, the tomb of I’timād-ud-Daulah is often regarded as a draft of the Tāj Mahal. Along with the main building, the structure consists of numerous outbuildings and gardens. The tomb, built between 1622 and 1628 represents a transition between the first phase of monumental Mughal architecture – primarily built from red sandstone with marble decorations, as in Humayun’s Tomb in Delhi and Akbar’s tomb in Sikandra – to its second phase, based on white marble and pietra dura inlay, most elegantly realized in the Tāj Mahal.
In the afternoon drive back to Delhi and on arrival we will drop you at your hotel or Delhi airport for your onward Journeys.

Bangalore and Mysore are among such places that reflect historical significance and cultural affluence.

Bangalore is the capital of Karnataka states and known as Silicon Valley of India” and also known as “The Garden City of India“. This is the 3rd most populated city of India. The foundation for Bangalore was laid Kempe Gowda, feudal ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire. It was also ruled by Maharajas of Mysore, Haider Ali and the British. There are several interesting tourist places to explore in Bangalore such as Bangalore palace, famous Temples and beautiful gardens.

Mysore is a very interesting place and also known as the historical capital of Karnataka. There are lots of thing to explore here as the grand palaces, rich flora and fauna and a tranquil environment. Our Bangalore Mysore Ooty packages could be a stress-free quick trip to this historical city of Mysore and modern city Bangalore. You can also explore the important things in Mysore such as silk sarees, sculptures, sandal wood products, Mysore betel leaves, Coffee powder, Mysore rosewood inlay artifacts, Mysore painting, Channapatna toys, and incense sticks.

Our 04 days Trip to Bangalore Mysore and Ooty itinerary takes you to a gratifying tour to Bangalore and Mysore. The major highlights of this tour package are exploring Tipu Sultan’s Palace and Ranganathaswamy Temple in Bangalore, visiting Chamundi, Devi Temple near Mysore, Krishnarajasagar Dam and Mysore Palace in Mysore and short trip to Dolphin’s Nose and Botanical Garden in Ooty.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.title: Arrive Bangalore - City Tour
paragraphs: On arrival at Bangalore airport/railway station, meet our representative and transfer you to your already booked hotel in Bangalore. Check in at the hotel and get ready for Bangalore city tour. In our city day tour, we will be visiting the Tipu’s Palace, Ulsoor Lake, Lal Bagh, Nandi or Bull Temple, Cubbon Park and Vidhana Soudha. In the evening, we will be visiting the museums and art galleries. Stay overnight at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.title: Bangalore - Mysore
paragraphs: Today, we will start our day a bit early and straightaway drive to Mysore. En-route, we will be visiting the Ranganathaswamy Temple and Srirangapatnam, which is the capital of Tipu Sultan, and Channapatna Toys Center. Thereafter, we will continue our journey to Mysore. On reaching, check in at the hotel and get freshen up. Thereafter, we will leave for the sightseeing tour of Mysore. In our day tour, we will be visiting the famous tourist destinations of Mysore. We will start our day tour by paying a visit to Krishnarajasagar Dam, Mysore Palace and Brindavan Gardens. Later in the evening, we will return back to the hotel for a relaxing overnight stay.

Mysore is a beautiful city located in Karnataka state at the base of the Chamundi Hills about 146 km southwest of Bangalore. It was the capital of the Kingdom of Mysore from 1399-1947. Today, it is counted among one of the cleanest city in India. Stay overnight at the Hotel

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.title: Mysore - Ooty
paragraphs: After breakfast in the morning, we will again proceed for Mysore city excursion tour. In today’s day tour, we will be visiting Zoological Gardens. This zoo is counted among the best in the country. Thereafter, we will head towards Shri Jayachamarajendra Art Gallery and St. Philomena’s Church that is raised in Gothic style. We will also visit the temple at Chamundi Hills, devoted to Goddess Chamundeshwari. She is the deity of the royal family of Mysore. In the evening, we will embark on the journey to Ooty also known as ”the Queen of hill stations’. On arrival, check in at the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.title: Ooty
paragraphs: In the morning after breakfast, we will leave to explore the real natural beauty of Ooty. We will start out day outing by visiting the Botanical Gardens, with a peaceful Lotus Pond that cover Dodda Betta. It is the highest peak of this hill station. Further, we will visit the tea estates, Dolphin’s Nose (a picnic spot), Lamb’s Rock, Ooty Lake, Kodanadu’s View Point and Catherine Falls. Later, we will return back to the hotel in Ooty for a relaxing overnight stay.

Ooty is a town situated 80 km north of Coimbatore. Nestled in the Nilgiri Hills, it is one of the famous hill station and a film shooting spot that attract visitors from across the country as well as the world. Stay overnight stay at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.title: Ooty - Bangalore airport
paragraphs: On the last day of our tour, we will have breakfast in the morning and check out from the hotel to drive back to Bangalore. On arrival, get transferred to the airport or railway station to catch the flight or board train for onward destination.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.title: Arrive Jaipur
paragraphs: Meeting and Assistance on arrival at Jaipur Airport and transfer to hotel with WTI Tours & Travels’ representative. Stay Overnight at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.title: Explore Jaipur City
paragraphs: Today after breakfast proceed for an excursion to Amber Fort, the palace complex which stands to this date was commenced under the reign of Raja Man Singh. The Amer Fort was built in red sandstone and marble and the Maotha Lake adds a certain charm to the entire Fort. Though the fort is quite old and may even look so from the outside, it is beautiful on the inside and boasts of various buildings of prominence like the ’Diwan-i-Aam’, the ’Sheesh Mahal’ and even the ’Sukh Mahal’. The Amer Fort has influences of both Hindu and Muslim architecture.
Here at Amber fort, we will enjoy the elephant ride that will be the most thrilling experience of your life.

After that we visit Jaigarh Fort, located on the Hill of Eagles, Jaigarh fort was built in 1726 AD by Sawan Jai Singh II. Jaigarh Fort is located at a height of 500 feet above sea level and offers panoramic views of the surrounding.

Later we will stop for photos at Jal Mahal (Water Palace). Tourist is not allowed to visit this palace from inside. It is a palace located in the middle of the Man Sagar Lake in Jaipur. The palace and the lake around it were renovated and enlarged in the 18th century by Maharaja Jai Singh II of Amber.

After that, will visit City Palace, a perfect blend of Rajasthani & Mughal architecture. The center of the palace is a seven-storied building called Chandra Palace, with fine views over the gardens & the city. Further we visit Jantar Mantar (Solar Observatory), an astronomical treasure house, with solar devices that give accurate predictions till date. We also visit Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds), a five-storied structure of pink sandstone. It was built in the year 1799 so that veiled royal women could peer down the busy street market unseen by the world through its 593 stone Jharokas (mini windows). Stay overnight at the Hotel

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.title: Jaipur - Pushkar - Jodhpur (5 Hrs Drive)
paragraphs: Today after breakfast drive to Jodhpur ”Blue City” of Rajathan, India. Jodhpur once the capital of the Marwar kingdom, Jodhpur retains its regal touch to this day.
On the Way we can stop for a short while and see the Pushkat Lake and Brahma Temple.
Continue drive to Jodhpur. Stay overnight at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.title: Jodhpur Sightseeing - Udaipur
paragraphs: Today after breakfast we will proceed for a half day city tour of “Blue City” Jodhpur visiting Mehranghar Fort, is one of the best forts in India with its exquisitely latticed windows, carved panels, elaborately adorned windows and walls of Moti Mahal, Phool Mahal, Sheesh Mahal. The Jaswant Thada, was built in 1899 by Maharaja Sardar Singh in commemoration of his father Maharaja Jaswant Singh II. Next, we can see Clock Tower is situated in one of the busiest areas of Jodhpur, the Sadar Bazaar.
In the afternoon drive to Udaipur – a Romantic City of Rajasthan, India. Udaipur, the city of lakes, was founded in 1559, and became the capital of Mewar kingdom thanks to the thriving trade market.
On the way we can see Ranakpur Temple. Stay overnight at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.title: Udaipur Sightseeing
paragraphs: Today after breakfast we will proceed for a city tour of Romantic City Udaipur visiting Fateh Sagar Lake, Pichola Lake, Sahelion ki Bari, Jagdish Temple & City palace.
Sunset boat cruise in Lake Pichola to see the Jagmandir.
Stay overnight at the Hotel

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.title: Udaipur - Mumbai (By Flight)
paragraphs: Today we will transfer you to Udaipur airport to board flight for Mumbai. Upon arrival transfer to hotel and check in. Stay overnight t the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.title: Mumbai Sightseeing
paragraphs: Morning excursion to Elephanta Caves (Elephanta Caves visit depend of the whether condition).

Later Local City Tour of Mumbai visiting Gateway of India overlooking the Harbor. Later drive past thru grand imposing High Court that are South Mumbai’s main architectural attraction, Bombay University Library, Victoria Terminus Train Station (CST) – UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Rajabai Tower, The Rajabai Clock Tower is modelled on the Big Ben in London. The tower was built by a wealthy businessman who dedicated it to his mother called Rajabai. St. Thomas Cathedral, This is the most beautiful church in Mumbai, located near Flora Fountain, South Mumbai.

Further we visit Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya, formerly known as the Prince of Wales Museum (Monday Closed) of Western India, is one of the premier art and history museum in India. The Museum building is a fine example of the Indo-Saracenic style of architecture and Mani Bhawan (Gandhi Museum), Mani Bhavan served as Mahatma Gandhi’s home when he used to visit Mumbai. Hanging Gardens and Kamala Nehru Park, Mumbai, These gardens are opposite each other in Malabar Hill Area of South Mumbai. The Hanging Gardens was built in 1880 atop a water storage reservoir. The garden is a haven for walkers and it has plant sculptures of various animals. Kamala Nehru Park offers a bird’s eye view of Chowpatty Beach and the Marine Drive Promenade.
Stay overnight at the Hotel

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.title: Arrive Paro - Thimphu
paragraphs: Welcome to Bhutan!. On arrival at Paro Airport, our representative will warmly welcome & greet you and we will drive to Thimphu, the capital city of Bhutan. The drive will take about 1 hour and 30 minutes along a river valley, past small villages and traditional farmhouses, through the sound of peaceful river flowing of Paa-chu and Thim-chu. It’s a small & charming capital city located in the heart of the Himalayas.
On arrival Thimphu, check in into Hotel. Overnight stay at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.title: Thimphu Sightseeing
paragraphs: Today after breakfast we will proceed for sightseeing of Thimphu visiting Memorial Chorten, built in 1974 in the memory of third king Jigme Dorji Wangchuk. Big Buddha Point is a gigantic Shakyamuni Buddha statue under construction in the mountains of Thimphu valley. The Buddha Dordenma is sited amidst the ruins of Kuensel Phodrang, the palace of Sherab Wangchuck, the thirteenth Druk Desi.

Later we can see Paper Factory, the Bhutanese Desho paper factory in Bhutan, weaving center, the hand woven clothes. Then, visit to Changgangkha temple, founded in 12th century by great Lama Phajo Drukgom Zhipo and visit to Drupthop nunnery, the place which was founded in 15th century and later built in the year 1976 by Reki Jigdrel.

Drive to Mothithang mini-zoo to see the National Animal of Bhutan (Takin). The Takin(Budorcas Taxicolor) as a National Animal of Bhutan is attributed to a legend of the animal’s creation in Bhutan in the 15th century by Lama Drukpa Kunley. Then hike to Sangyegang Cross hike, the hike will take around 1 hour and 30 minutes through the beautiful pine forest. Through this hike, we can see the beautiful valley Thimphu city.

Evening, stroll around Thimphu city, visit to Tashichho Dzong, seat of the National Government and the Central Monastic Body, including the summer residence of the Je Khenpo (Chief Abbot of Bhutan). Dinner and overnight stay at Thimphu hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.title: Thimphu -Wangdi/Punakha
paragraphs: Today after breakfast we will drive to Wangdi/Punakha, over Dochula, 3150m above the sea level. While reaching at Dochula, if the weather is clear you can see the Himalayan Mountains of Bhutan including the highest mountain of Bhutan, the Gankar Puensum (7554m), which is the unclimbed mountain in Bhutan.

On reaching at Lobesa, hike to Chimme Lhakhang, which was founded in 15th century by Devin madman Drukpa Kuenley. The hike will take around 1hour and 30minutes for too and forth. Then, we will continue our journey to Punakha, on reaching at Punakha, visit to Punakha Dzong, the seat of the administrative system and the Central Monastic Body, including the winter residence of the Je Khenpo (Chief Abbot of Bhutan). Evening at leisure.
Overnight stay at the Hotel

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.title: Wangdi Phodrang/Punakha-Phobjikha (Day Excursion)
paragraphs: After breakfast, drive to Phobjikha valley, over Lawala Pass, 3280m above the sea level. The Phobjika Valley is the winter roosting place for the Black-necked Cranes – visit central Bhutan to roost, circling the monastery three times on arrival and repeating this circling when returning to Tibet. Before reaching at Lawala pass, if we turn back when the weather is clear, we can see the second highest mountain of Bhutan, Jhomolhari (7454m). The drive will take around 3hours to reach at Phobjikha valley. In winter, we can see the yaks around these passes.

On reaching at Phobjikha, visit to Gangtey Monastery, is an important monastery of two main center Nyingmapa school of Buddhism in the country. The main seat of the religious tradition based on Pema Lingpa tradition. The Monastery’s history traces to the early 17th century and back to the prophecies made by the well-known Terton (treasure finder) Pema Lingpa in the late 15th century. Then, hike to Gantey Natural trail, the hike will take around 1 hour and 40 minutes through the blue pine trees. Lunch will be serving at Phobjikha. After having lunch, we will drive back to Wandi/Punakha. Overnight stay at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.title: Wangdi/Punakha-Paro
paragraphs: Today after breakfast, we will drive back to Paro over Dochula passes, 3150m above the sea level. The drive will take around 4hours to reach at Paro and lunch will be on the way to Paro.

On reaching at Paro, visit to Paro Rimpung Dzong, the center of civil and religious authority in this region. The original structure was built in the year 1646 by the great unifier of Bhutan Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyel. Evening stroll around Paro town. Overnight stay at the Hotel

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.title: Paro-Haa (Day Excursion)
paragraphs: After having breakfast, we will drive to Haa through the Chelela pass, 3880m above the sea level. From these pass also, if the weather is clear we can see the second highest mountain of Bhutan the Jhomolhari, 7454m above the sea level. The drive will take around 3hours and 30 minutes and lunch will be serving at Haa.

On reaching at Haa, visit to Lhakhang Karpo and Lhakhang Nagkpo founded in 7th century by 33th king of Tibet, Songtsen Gampo. After this we will make round of Haa town and we will drive back to Paro. Overnight stay at Hotel in Paro.

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.title: Paro
paragraphs: Today after breakfast, we will make a hike to Paro Taktshang Monastery, the most famous and sacred monastery in Bhutan. Taktshang means “TigerNest” named after Guru Rinpoche reportedly flew to this site riding on the back of a flying tigress in the 8th century. We have to walk about 2 hours and 30 minutes up steep from the road end. The trail climbs through beautiful pine forest, many of the trees festooned with Spanish moss, and an occasional grove of fluttering prayer flags. Lunch will be served at Taktshang cafeteria.

While coming back, visit Kyichu Lhakhang, it is one of the two most sacred and the oldest temples in Bhutan, built in 7th century by Tibetan king Songtsen Gampo (the 33rd Tibetan king, who is also the manifestation of avoloketeshivara, commonly known to Bhutanese as Chenrize).
Evening at leisure, dinner and overnight stay.

itinerary.label: Day 8
itinerary.title: Paro - Departure
paragraphs: Today after breakfast, we will transfer you to Paro airport to board flight for your onward Destination. We wish you a very safe and pleasant flight for your onward destinations.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.title: Explore Pink City Jaipur
paragraphs: In the morning visit the Amber Fort ascend fort on open jeep or enjoy Elephant Rides. Amber was the ancient capital of Kachhawaha dynasty for long time ago. It was moved to newly created Jaipur. Visit the Sheesh Mahal (Hall of victory) which is a hall glittering with mirrors.
Afternoon visit Maharaja’s City Palace, the Observatory and drive past to Hawa Mahal. Evening transfer to hotel or free for shopping. Overnight stay at hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.title: Jaipur - Agra (4.5 Hrs Drive)
paragraphs:
After breakfast drive to Agra. En route stop at Fatehpur Sikri. Fatehpur Sikri was built by Akbar, the Mughal emperor between 1571 and 1585. It is one of the finest examples of Mughal architectural splendour. It was constructed mainly as a tribute to the great Sufi saint Shaikh Salim Chisti who had blessed Akbar with a son. Though the city is in ruins, it is a must visit place for those who visit Agra.

On arrival at Agra our representative will assist in your check in process at the hotel. Overnight stay at hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.title: Agra

Morning visit the famous Taj Mahal in sunrise, built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. This monument is made of white marble and it took 22 years to get constructed.

Afternoon visit the Agra Fort which has the Pearl Mosque, Diwan-e-am (the hall of public audience) and Diwan-e-Khas (the hall of private audience). Overnight stay at hotel.

paragraphs: After breakfast transfer to Agra Railway station to catch a train for Jhansi. Meet on arrival at Jhansi Railway station and drive straight to Khajuraho, en route optional stopover at Orchha.

”Orchha”, meaning ”hidden” was the hallmark of Bundela dynasty. The origin of Bundelas goes back to the 11th century. It is believed that it was founded by a Rajput prince who offered himself in sacrifice to the mountain goddess, Vrindavasini. The goddess stopped the prince from sacrificing and named him Bundela (meaning the one who offered blood). The Bundelas ruled over this area between the river Yamuna and Narmada.
On arrival at Khajuraho our representative will assist in your check in process at the hotel. Evening enjoy Sound and Light show at Khajuraho. Overnight stay at hotel.

After attaining enlightenment, the Buddha came to Sarnath where he gave his first sermon and visit the deer park (he delivered his first sermon, or in religious language, set in motion the wheel of Law (maha- Dharmachakra Pravartan). This road trip gives you a chance to see the country side and also you can meet local and village people. It takes approx 3 hrs to reach Agra by surface.

itinerary.label: 10:00 AM
itinerary.title: Arrival in Agra City and visit Taj Mahal
paragraphs: Once you arrive in Agra, you will meet with our professional Tour Guide and he will escorted you to Taj Mahal.

Taj Mahal is located in the historical city of Agra. It was built by the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan as a memorial for his third wife, Mumtaz Mahal. Constructed entirely out of white marble in the 17th century, it is among the finest edifices of Mughal architecture. Recognised by the UNESCO as a world heritage site, this monument is also considered to be one of the seven wonders of the modern world. Every year visitors numbering more than the entire population of Agra pass through the magnificent gates to catch a glimpse of this breathtaking monument, and only a few leave disappointed. Shah Jahan said about the Taj that it made ”the sun and the moon shed tears from their eyes”.

itinerary.label: 12: 00 PM
itinerary.title: Visit Agra Fort
paragraphs: Agra Fort was built in the year 1573 under the reign of Akbar – one of the greatest Mughal Emperors. Akbar built the fort to make it the main residence of the Mughals. The fort remained as the main residence of the emperors belonging to the Mughal dynasty until the year 1638. The fort houses numerous impressive structures like the Jahangir Mahal, Khas Mahal, Diwan-i-Khass, Diwan-i-Am, Machchhi Bhawan and Moti Masjid. In 1638, the capital of the Mughal dynasty was moved from Agra to Delhi, causing the Agra Fort to lose its status as the main residence of the Mughal emperors. The fort is separated from its sister monument Taj Mahal by just 2.5 kilometers. Often described as the walled city, Agra Fort is a UNESCO World Heritage site. Today, the fort is a major tourist spot and attracts many tourists from all over the world.

itinerary.label: 01: 00 PM
itinerary.title: Lunch Break
paragraphs: After seeing the Agra Fort, we will have a lunch break. Plenty of nice restaurant available in Agra and specialized in Mughlai cousin, continental, and indian cousin.

itinerary.label: 02:00 PM
itinerary.title: Visit Baby Taj
paragraphs: ”Baby Taj” The Itmad-ud-Daulah’s Tomb is one of the most impressive architectural wonders of the city of Agra. This monument is considered to be the inspiration behind the Taj Mahal. For this fact it is known as the “Baby Taj Mahal”. Many tourists that visit Agra for the Taj Mahal also look for the Itmad-ud-Daulah’s Tomb.

Despite the similarities, the tomb of Itimad-Ud-Daulah is considered a more delicate artwork than Taj Mahal, with marble lattice screens and fine carvings. This was the first of many tombs to be erected on the banks of River Yamuna.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.title: Bangalore - Shravanabelagola – Belur/ Halebid –Hassan
paragraphs: Morning after breakfast, check out the hotel and drive to Shravanabelagola, one of the most important pilgrimage destinations in Jainism. The 57 feet tall statue of Gommateshvara Bahubali is main attraction of Shravanabelagola. Then drive to Belur and Halebid, two tiny but beautiful heritage towns located in Hassan district. Belur and Halebid are home to several exquisite temples which reveal the artistry of Indian.

Halebid :- Visit to Halebid, the 12th century capital of the Hoysalas. The Hoysaleswara temple was built during this time by Ketamala and attributed to Vishnuvardhana, the Hoysala ruler. Halebid enshrines Hoysaleswara and Shantaleswara, named after the temple builder Vishnuvardhana Hoysala and his wife, Queen Shantala.

Belur:- Chennakesava Temple built by the Hoysala King Vishnuvardhana in 1117 A D to commemorate his conversion from Jainism to Vaishnavism. The temple took 103 years to build and is a classic example of the Hoysala style. Standing on a star-shaped platform, it has three doorways and bracket figures or ’Madanikas’ representing the masterpieces of craftsmanship. The pillars of the temple are richly carved. The Channekeshava Temple is unique as it is said that every Hindu deity has been represented in the temple.
Veeranarayana temple Situated on the west of the Chenna Kesava Temple is Veeranarayana temple. This temple houses the shrines of Kappe Chenniga, Andal, Saumya Nayaki, and other deities.
On arrival transfer to Hotel. Overnight at the Hotel.

The Temples, Palaces, Tombs, Military warehouses, Cenotaphs, natural landscaped locations and above all its 3-layer fort wall with bastions are mute witnesses for a bygone era of glorious days. The place is known for its noted 17 metre high image of Lord Gomateshvara on the top of Indragiri hill. Overnight at the hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.title: Delhi Sightseeing
paragraphs: Breakfast at Hotel. You will proceed for Guided full day city tour of Old Delhi and New Delhi:-

INDIA GATE (War memorial Site);- The India Gate, originally called the All India War Memorial, is a war memorial located astride the Rajpath, on the eastern edge of the ‘ceremonial axis’ of New Delhi, formerly called Kingsway. Almost similar to its French counterpart, it commemorates the 70,000 Indian soldiers who lost their lives fighting for the British Army during the World War I. The memorial bears the names of more than 13,516 British and Indian soldiers killed in the Northwestern Frontier in the Afghan war of 1919.
Later drive past through President House & the Parliament.

JAMA MASJID (India’s large Mosque):- This great mosque of Old Delhi is the largest in India, with a courtyard capable of holding 25,000 devotees. It was begun in 1644 and ended up being the final architectural extravagance of Shah Jahan, the Mughal emperor who built the Taj Mahal and the Red Fort.

RED FORT (drive past through);- The Red Fort (Lal Quila) in Delhi, India was originally built by the fifth Emperor of India’s Mughal Dynasty, Shahjahan in 1639, when he moved India’s capital from Agra to Delhi.
The Red Fort, which derives its name from the red sandstone bricks which make up its protective walls, was built as Shahjahan’s new palace and as a defensive structure.

In the afternoon visit QUTAB MINAR :- Qutub Minar, also known as Qutab Minar and Qutab Minar, is the tallest minaret in India, originally an ancient Islamic Monument, inscribed with Arabic inscriptions, though the iron pillar has some Brahmi inscriptions.

HUMAYUN’S TOMB: – Humayun died in 1556, and his widow Hamida Banu Begam, also known as Haji Begam, commenced the construction of his tomb in 1569, fourteen years after his death. It is the first distinct example of proper Mughal style, which was inspired by Persian architecture. It is well known that Humayun picked up the principles of Persian architecture during his exile, and he himself is likely to have planned the tomb, although there is no record to that effect. Mirak Mirza Ghiyath, a Persian, was the architect employed by Haji Begam for this tomb.

paragraphs: Today we will proceed for Agra, beautifully situated on the banks of river Yamuna. On arrival transfer to Hotel and check in.
In the afternoon half day Guided city tour of Agra visiting Agra Fort and Baby Taj.
Overnight stay at Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.title: Agra - Ranthambore (6 Hrs drive)ive)
paragraphs: Sunrise we will visit to Taj Mahal, a symbol of eternal love, which stands on the banks of River Yamuna. It was built by the 5th Mughal emperor, Shah Jehan in the memory of his wife, Mumtaz Mahal. It was completed in 22 years with the orders of Shah Jahan and it was dedicated to Mumtaz Mahal (Arjumand Bano Begum), the wife of Shah. 20.000 workers labored and 32 crore rupees were spent during the construction of the monument and it was built according to Islamic architecture.
Back to hotel for the Breakfast.

After breakfast check out from hotel and leave for Ranthambore. Ranthambore National Park is one of the largest national parks in northern India. Ranthambore National Park is probably the best place in the world to see wild Indian tigers in its only dry deciduous natural habitat. Tigers can be easily spotted even during the day time. Ranthambore is also known for famous heritage site due to ruins and Fort. It is a home for different species of animals and birds.
On arrival transfer Hotel and check in. Stay Overnight at Hotel.

paragraphs: once again the game drive at Ranthambore National Park. Later drive to Jaipur . Upon arrival check into hotel. Overnight at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.title: Explore Jaipur City
paragraphs: Today we take an excursion to Amber Fort, the palace complex which stands to this date was commenced under the reign of Raja Man Singh. The Amer Fort was built in red sandstone and marble and the Maotha Lake adds a certain charm to the entire Fort. Though the fort is quite old and may even look so from the outside, it is beautiful on the inside and boasts of various buildings of prominence like the ’Diwan-i-Aam’, the ’Sheesh Mahal’ and even the ’Sukh Mahal’. The Amer Fort has influences of both Hindu and Muslim architecture. We take an Elephant ride to reach the Fort situated on the hill, an overwhelming experience.

Later we will visit City Palace, a perfect blend of Rajasthani & Mughal architecture. The center of the palace is a seven-storied building called Chandra Palace, with fine views over the gardens & the city. Further we visit Jantar Mantar (Solar Observatory), an astronomical treasure house, with solar devices that give accurate predictions till date. We also visit Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds), a five-storied structure of pink sandstone. The cenotaph of Maharaja Jaswant Singh holds the rare portraits of the rulers and Maharajas of Jodhpur. A visit inside the cenotaphs, with some villagers of the region, would bring forward the reverence they still hold for their brave kings. Overnight at the Hotel.

paragraphs: Breakfast at Hotel. Morning drive to Udaipur and on the way visit Ranakpur Temple.
Ranakpur Jain temple (open at 1200 hours). Ranakpur the 15th century Chaumukh Jain temple, one of the most beautiful crafted sculpted temples in India.

The Ranakpur Temple is one of the most famous Jain temples in Rajasthan and dedicated to the first Jain Tirthankar (enlightened human) of our time cycle, Adinath (aka Lord Rishabha). It is a very big temple (ceiling around 7m high), constructed of white marble. paragraphs: Today early morning we will transfer you to New Delhi Railway station to Board Amritsar Shatabdi Express (Dept. Delhi @ 07:00 Hrs/ Arrive Amritsar @ 13:00 Hrs). Meeting and assistance on arrival at Amritsar railway Station and transfer to Hotel with our Office’s representative.

In the evening around 5 PM, we will proceed for Wagah border. Here, watch the lowering of the flags ceremony, which takes place each evening before sunset. Also referred to as the ‘Beating Retreat border ceremony on the international level,’ this daily military ritual has been practiced by both India and Pakistan – the Border Security Force and the Pakistan Rangers – since 1959. Witness the brash parade of soldiers from both sides of the Wagah border, which once served as the only road linking the two countries. Overnight stay at the Hotel

itinerary.label: Day 8
itinerary.title: Amritsar Sightseeing - Departure
paragraphs: Today after breakfast, embark on a sightseeing tour of the old city of Amritsar with your tour guide. Begin with a morning visit to Golden Temple, considered the Sikhs’ spiritual and cultural center. Amritsar, meaning ‘pool of nectar,’ was founded in 1579 by Guru Ram Das – the fourth Guru of the Sikh religion. At the Golden Temple, set amid a pool of holy water, visitors and devotees from all faiths are welcome. You’ll get a glimpse of the Sikh temple tradition of offering daily Guru-Ka-Langar – a free, community meal that began in the 16th century. As you watch the community kitchen feed up to 10,000 people, learn about this Sikh principle of equality and the practice of eating together.

Jallianwala Bagh, a public garden within the city and the site of a notorious massacre of Indians under British rule in 1919. Next, visit the beautiful Ram Bagh Gardens and the remains of Maharaja Ranjit Singh’s summer palace – now a national museum.
Durgiana Temple: A partial replica of the Golden Temple, the Durgiana temple is situated outside the Lohgarh Gate. It is dedicated to the Goddess Durga and is frequented by devout Hindus.
In the late afternoon we can transfer you to Airport to board flight for Delhi. On arrival in Delhi catch your onward International flight for back to home with sweet memories!!.

intro: Golden Triangle with Haridwar and Rishikesh Tour will take you through the historical and cultural places of North India as Delhi, Jaipur and Agra and then get a feel of the spiritual ethos of India. A paradise for nature lovers, Haridwar or the Gateway to God presents a kaleidoscope of Indian culture and civilization. It is also the starting point on the journey to the sacred sources of the rivers Ganga and Yamuna.

Haridwar and Rishikesh Tour Packages includes two famous holy places of India, located quite close to one another and the River Ganges crossed each other. In Haridwar there are several Hindu temples in every possible corner. Since Haridwar is a place of pilgrimage to many people in the country, visited millions of people every year. Rishikesh is blessed by nature and situated at a higher altitude. Both Places are located by the roaring Ganges, whereas the calmness of Ganga locates Haridwar. It is known more because of the spiritual and religious impact it has on the tourists.

Rishikesh is known as the “World Capital of Yoga” and also “Place of Sagas” . It is a spiritual located at the confluence of the Chandrabhaga and Ganga and surrounded by scenic beauty of the hills on three sides. In the recent past this place has become a favorite destination of spiritual seekers and yoga practitioners. Also, Rishikesh is the place where most travellers start their Char Dham Yatra. Apart from the scenic beauty, Rishikesh is quite famous in adventure activities like river rafting, paragliding, and many more.

Apart from that, Haridwar’s Evening Aarti is very famous not only in India but all around the world. The magnificent Ganga Aarti that takes place in the Har-Ki-Pauri Ghat is another reason why so many people visit Haridwar quite frequently.

paragraphs: After Breakfast we will proceed for a Guided City Tour of Old and New Delhi visiting Laxmi Narayan Temple, also known as Birla Mandir, India Gate, memorial built in the year 1931 to commemorate the Indian soldiers who died in the World War I & the Afghan Wars. Drive Pass Thru President’s House, Parliament Building, Diplomatic Enclave..etc

Later we will visit Old Delhi, with the great Jama Masjid, Built in the year 1656 AD by the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan, it is the largest & best known mosque in India. Rickshaw Rides in Narrow lane of Chandni Chowk Bazaar in Old Delhi. Next we can see Raj Ghat, memorial to the Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi.

In the afternoon we will visit Humayun’s Tomb, memorial of Mughal Emperor Humayun, built in the year 1562. Qutub Minar built in the year 1206 by Qutub-ud-din Aibek. It is an important example of Indo-Islamic Architecture. Lotus Temple (Bahai Temple): this temple is built in the shape of a lotus flower and is the last of seven Major Bahai’s temples built around the world. Stay Overnight at the Hotel

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.title: Delhi - Jaipur (5 Hrs Drive)
paragraphs: Today we drive to Jaipur ” Pink City” of Rajasthan.
Upon arrival transfer to Hotel and check in.
Evening take a round of Old Jaipur city and watch the Aarti Ceremony in Birla Temple to understand the culture and Custom.
Stay overnight at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.title: Explore Jaipur City
paragraphs: Today after breakfast we will proceed for a Guided City Tour of Pink City Jaipur visiting Amber Fort, was built in red sandstone and marble and the Maotha Lake adds a certain charm to the entire Fort.Beautiful on the inside and boasts of various buildings of prominence like the ’Diwan-i-Aam’, the ’Sheesh Mahal’ and even the ’Sukh Mahal’. The Amer Fort has influences of both Hindu and Muslim architecture.
We can enjoy Elephant ride to reach the Fort situated on the hill, an overwhelming experience.

Later we will visit City Palace, a perfect blend of Rajasthani & Mughal architecture. Jantar Mantar (Solar Observatory), an astronomical treasure house, with solar devices that give accurate predictions till date. We stop for Photos at Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds), a five-storied structure of pink sandstone. It was built in the year 1799 so that veiled royal women could peer down the busy street market unseen by the world through its 593 stone Jharokas (mini windows).
Stay overnight at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.title: Agra - Jaipur (5 Hrs Drive)
paragraphs: Today we drive to Agra. Agra is a city where the prefect romantic allure can be found. The land to the Taj Mahal, the Symbol of Love and one of the Seven Wonders of the World, makes the air of Agra full of love and romance. While the Legacy of Mughal Empire just didn’t gave Taj Mahal to this romantic land but many other mesmerizing attractions worth exploring as well.
On the way we can see Abhaneri Step Well and Fatehpur Sikri Fort.
Stay overnight at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.title: Agra Sightseeine)g - Delhi (3.5 Hrs Drive)
paragraphs: Today morning we will see first the Taj Mahal in Sunrise.
Back to Hotel for Breakfast. Post Breakfast we will see Agra Fort and the Tomb of Itmad – Ud – Daula.
After that we drive back to Delhi. Stay overnight at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.title: Delhi - Cochin (By Flight)
paragraphs: Today morning transfer you to airport for flight to Cochin.
Upon arrival transfer to hotel and check in.

Later proceed for sightseeing tour of Cochin visiting Chinese Fishing nets, Fort Cochin, Mattancherry, Old Spice market at Mattancherry St. Francis Church, Dutch Cemetery, the Dutch Palace (Friday Closed), Hill palace, Bolghatty Palace & Jewish Synagogue.

In the evening we will proceed to see Kathakali Dance Show, The Kathakali dance is presented in a group, the themes of which are based on Hindu Mythologies – particularly on epics – Ramayana and Mahabharata. Here Kathakali, music, martial arts and other dance forms are demonstrated in traditional style with its real sence and reality. We hearty invites you to be a part of our rich culture and experience the world’s one of the greatest art forms. Stay Overnight stay at Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 8
itinerary.title: Cochin - Munnar (3.5 Hrs drive)
paragraphs: After breakfast we drive to Munnar, the Fascinating Hill Station of South India – Munnar. On the way we will visit Spice Plantation.
Stay overnight at the Hotel

itinerary.label: Day 9
itinerary.title: Explore Munnar
paragraphs: After leisurely Breakfast. We will proceed for the sightseeing tour of Munnar visiting Eravikulam National Park – the natural habitat of the Ibex called Nilgiri Tahar, Mattupetty Lake and Dam, Tea Plantation and Munnar town. Stay overnight at Hotel

itinerary.label: Day 10
itinerary.title: Munnar - Thekkady (3 hrs drive)
paragraphs: Today we drive to Thekkady / Periyar. Periyar (Thekkady) Wildlife Sanctuary is one of the well maintained wildlife sanctuaries of South India and it spreads out over an area of 777 sq kms. The splendid artificial lake formed by the Mullaperiyar dam across the Periyar river adds to the charm of the park. This is the only sanctuary in India where you can have the unique experience of viewing wildlife at close quarters from the safety of a boat on the lake. The rest of the afternoon is free or stroll through the bustling spice market of Kumili village.
On arrival transfer to hotel and check in.
In the afternoon we will proceed for Boat ride on Lake Periyar where one can have a unique experience of viewing wildlife at close quarters from the safety of a boat on the lake.
Overnight stay at Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 11
itinerary.title: Thekkady - Alleppey (4 Hrs drive)
paragraphs: After Breakfast we will leave for Alleppey and on arrival we will board on Air-Conditioned Deluxe House boat for an Overnight Back Water Cruise for Alleppey round. The Backwaters of Kerala is a network of interconnected canals, rivers, lakes and inlets formed by more than 900 km of waterways. The backwaters have a unique ecosystem – freshwater from the rivers meets the seawater from the Arabian Sea.

House Boats have all the creature comforts of a good hotel including furnished bedrooms, modern toilets, cozy living rooms, a kitchen and even a balcony for angling. Parts of the curved roof of wood or plaited palm open out to provide shade and allow uninterrupted views. Stay overnight in House Boat.

itinerary.label: Day 12
itinerary.title: Alleppey - Cochin Airport(3 Hrs drive)
paragraphs: Today after breakfast we will disembark from house boat at 10 am and drop you at Cochin airport to board flight for your onward destination.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.title: Arrive Delhi
paragraphs: Meeting and assistance upon arrival at Delhi airport and Transfer to Hotel with our office’s representative. Stay overnight at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.title: Delhi Sightseeing
paragraphs: After breakfast we will proceed for a Guided city tour of Old and New Delhi city tour visiting India Gate, memorial built in the year 1931 to commemorate the Indian soldiers who died in the World War I & the Afghan Wars. The names of the soldiers who died in these wars are inscribed on the walls. President’s House, the official residence of the President of India, built in the year 1931.

Later we will visit Old Delhi, the 17th century walled city of Shah Jahanabad, Visiting the great Jama Masjid, the principal mosque of Old Delhi. Built in the year 1656 AD by the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan, it is the largest & best known mosque in India. Later we walk down through Chandni Chowk, the old marketplace of Shah Jahanabad now a picturesque bazaar to reach Red Fort, built in the year 1648 by Shah Jehan. Later we visit Raj Ghat, memorial to the Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi. It is a simple black marble platform that marks the spot of his cremation20on 31 January 1948.

In the afternoon we will visit Humayun’s Tomb, memorial of Mughal Emperor Humayun, built in the year 1562. Qutub Minar built in the year 1206 by Qutub-ud-din Aibek. It is an important example of Indo-Islamic Architecture. Qutub Minar & its monuments are listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Lotus Temple (Bahai Temple): this temple is built in the shape of a lotus flower and is the last of seven Major Bahai’s temples built around the world. The architect Furiburz Sabha chose the lotus as the symbol common to Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and Islam. Stay overnight at Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.title: Delhi - Jaipur (5 Hrs Drive)
paragraphs: Today after breakfast we will leave for Jaipur ” Pink City” of Rajasthan.
Upon arrival transfer to Hotel and check in.
Evening take a round of Pink City and watch the Aarti ceremoney in Birla Temple. Stay Overnight at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.title: Jaipur Sightseeing
paragraphs: Today after early breakfast we will proceed for a Guided city tour of Pink City Jaipur visiting Amber Fort, the palace complex which stands to this date was commenced under the reign of Raja Man Singh. The Amer Fort was built in red sandstone and marble and the Maotha Lake adds a certain charm to the entire Fort. It is beautiful on the inside and boasts of various buildings of prominence like the ’Diwan-i-Aam’, the ’Sheesh Mahal’ and even the ’Sukh Mahal’. The Amer Fort has influences of both Hindu and Muslim architecture.
We can take an Elephant ride to reach the Fort situated on the hill, an overwhelming experience.

Later we will visit City Palace, a perfect blend of Rajasthani & Mughal architecture. The center of the palace is a seven-storied building called Chandra Palace, with fine views over the gardens & the city. Further we visit Jantar Mantar (Solar Observatory), an astronomical treasure house, with solar devices that give accurate predictions till date. We also visit Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds), a five-storied structure of pink sandstone. It was built in the year 1799 so that veiled royal women could peer down the busy street market unseen by the world through its 593 stone Jharokas (mini windows). Overnight at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.title: Jaipur - Agra ( 5 Hrs Drive)
paragraphs: Morning drive to Agra. Agra, beautifully situated on the banks of river Yamuna. It achieved prominence as the capital of the Mughal Emperors from the year 1526 to 1628, remains major tourist destination because of its many splendid Mughal-era monuments, most notably the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort & Fatehpur Sikri, all three are UNESCO World Heritage sites.
On the way we can see Abhaneri Step Well and also Fatehpur Sikri. Stay overnight at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.title: Agra - Delhi (3.5 Hrs Drive)
paragraphs: Sunrise we will visit to Taj Mahal, a symbol of eternal love, which stands on the banks of River Yamuna. It was built by the 5th Mughal emperor, Shah Jehan in the memory of his wife, Mumtaz Mahal. It was completed in 22 years with the orders of Shah Jahan and it was dedicated to Mumtaz Mahal (Arjumand Bano Begum), the wife of Shah. 20.000 workers labored and 32 crore rupees were spent during the construction of the monument and it was built according to Islamic architecture
Back to hotel for the Breakfast.
After Breakfast check out from Hotel and visit Agra Fort.

Agra Fort, is a UNESCO World Heritage site located in Agra, India. The fort is also known as Lal Qila, Fort Rouge and Red Fort of Agra. It is about 2.5 km northwest of its much more famous sister monument, the Taj Mahal. The fort can be more accurately described as a walled palatial city. It was constructed by the third Mughal emperor Akbar on the remains of an ancient site known as Badalgarh. Some of the exquisite structures that deserve a mention are: Sheesh Mahal, the Diwan-i-Am, Diwan-i-Khas, the Anguri Bagh, Khas Mahal, Mina Masjid, Nagina Masjid and Musamman Burj – A large, octagonal tower with a balcony facing the Taj Mahal.
Also we can see Baby Taj. In the late afternoon drive back to Delhi. Upon arrival transfer to Hotel and check in. Stay Overnight at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.title: Delhi - Varanasi ( By Flight)
paragraphs: Today after breakfast we will transfer you to Delhi airport to board flight for Varanasi.
Upon arrival in Varanasi, meet and greet with our office’s representative and transfer to Hotel and check in.

In the afternoon we take an excursion to Sarnath. After the Bouddha attained enlightenment in Bodh Gaya he came to Sarnath. Here in the Deer Park, he delivered his first sermon, or in religious language, set in motion the wheel of Law (maha- Dharmachakra Pravartan). On the day before his death Buddha included Sarnath along with Lumbini, Bodh Gaya and Kushinagar as the four places he thought to be sacred to his followers. The Emperor Ashoka, who spread the Buddha’s message of love and compassion throughout his vast empire, visited Sarnath around 234BC, and erected a stupa here. Several Buddhist structures were raised at Sarnath between the 3rd century BC and the 11th century AD, and today it presents the most expansive ruins amongst places on the Buddhist trail. Sarnath is 10 km from the holy city of Varanasi, and is an exceedingly tranqiuil place. The ruins, the museum and temple are all within walking distance.
Overnight stay at the Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 8
itinerary.title: Varanasi Sightseeing
paragraphs: Early morning boat rides on the holy river Ganges to view the sunrise where the Hindus perform their morning prayers. Back to Hotel for the Breakfast. Later proceed for half day city tour of Varanasi, visiting Bharat Mata temple, and Banaras Hindu University, Vishwanath Temple, Hanuman Temple, and Old City market.

Evening watchGanga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat in Varanasi. The Aarti takes place facing the river. The lamps are lit and circled around by the pandits (Hindu priests) in a clockwise manner, accompanied by changing or songs in praise of Mother Ganga. The idea is that the lamps acquire the power of the deity. After the ritual is complete, devotees will cup their hands over the flame and raise their palms to their forehead in order to get the Goddess’s purification and blessing. Stay overnight at Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 9
itinerary.title: Varanasi - Delhi (By Flight)
paragraphs: Today we will transfer you to Varanasi airport to board flight for Delhi in order to catch your international flight for back to Home.

Celebrated author Mark Twain, who visited India in the last decade of the 19th century, described the city as “older than history, older than tradition, older even than legend.”

Delhi where you would visit the picturesque attractions. Agra is renowned in the world because of the Mughal Heritage Wonder “Taj Mahal”. Taj Mahal is one of the universally admired masterpieces of the world’s heritage. Jaipur is another notable gem of the Heritage and Cultural India Tours. Owing to a number of forts and palaces, the ‘Pink City’ remains on the bucket list of avid travelers. Hawa Mahal, Amber Fort and a multitude of heritage hotels are worthy of admiration. Vibrant costumes and scrumptious cuisines will make your trip a memorable one.

Khajuraho is famous for its Erotic Temple- refers to Kamasutra (Western and Eastern Group of Temples). The temples at Khajuraho were built during the Chandella dynasty, which reached its apogee between 950 and 1050. Only about 20 temples remain; they fall into three distinct groups and belong to two different religions – Hinduism and Jainism. They strike a perfect balance between architecture and sculpture. The Temple of Kandariya is decorated with a profusion of sculptures that are among the greatest masterpieces of Indian art.

paragraphs: Morning transfer to airport to board flight to Aurangabad. On arrival meet and assist with our office’s representative and transfer to Hotel. Later proceed for half day excursion to Ellora (30 km/45 mins). Ellora Caves: Finest specimen of cave temple architecture in the world. Impressive on their own, these rock-hewn temples & monasteries lie just 30km away from Aurangabad city. They contain elaborate facades & exquisitely adorned interiors. These structures represent three ancient religious faiths: Hinduism, Buddhism & Jainism. In total, there are 34 cave temples & can be divided into three groups belonging roughly to three periods: Mahayana Buddhism (550-750 AD) 12 caves, Hinduism (600-875 AD) 17 caves & Jainism (800-1000 AD) 5 caves. (ELLORA CAVES IS CLOSED ON TUESDAY). Overnight at the Hotel

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.title: Aurangabad
paragraphs: Morning proceed for full day excursion to Ajanta (90 km/02 hrs). Ajanta Caves: Nestling in the inner fold of Sahyadri hills, 100 kms from Aurangabad in the shape of a mammoth horse- shoe are 30 rock caves of Ajanta, dating from 2nd century BC. Caves were discovered in the year 1819 by a group of British officers. It took around 600 years to create & carve marvellous statues in these caves with little more than a hammer & chisel. Ajanta, once the retreat of the Buddhist monastic orders features several ”chaityas” & viharas. Exquisite paintings & sculptures of Buddha’s life belong to the Mahayana period. In the evening drive back to Aurangabad. (AJANTA CAVES IS CLOSED ON MONDAY).Overnight at Hotel.

Kerala is blessed with a unique set of geographical features that have made it one of the most sought after tourist destinations in Asia. A long shoreline with serene beaches, tranquil stretches of emerald backwaters, lush hill stations and exotic wildlife. These are just a few of the wonders that await you once you crossover to the other side.

We start the Kerala Trip with Kochi sightseeing journey. Next, head over to Munnar and visit the local tea and spice plantations. After a two-day tour of Munnar, head over to Thekkady, where you can see some of the most exotic birds, animals and plants that Kerala has to offer. Finally, head over to the Venice of India and spend an entire day enjoying the luxury of a houseboat. Reach out to us for Kerala tourism packages and Kerala sightseeing trips with friends or family.

We hearty invites you to be a part of our rich culture and experience the world’s one of the greatest art forms.

Unending expanse of tea plantations – pristine valleys and mountains- exotic species of flora and fauna in its wild sanctuaries and forests – aroma of spice scented cool air – yes! Munnar has all these and more.
On arrival check-in to the hotel. Stay overnight at Hotel

The splendid artificial lake formed by the Mullaperiyar dam across the Periyar river adds to the charm of the park. This is the only sanctuary in India where you can have the unique experience of viewing wildlife at close quarters from the safety of a boat on the lake. The rest of the afternoon is free or stroll through the bustling spice market of Kumili village.
On arrival transfer to hotel and check in.

Overnight stay at Hotel.

The backwaters have a unique ecosystem – freshwater from the rivers meets the seawater from the Arabian Sea.

House Boats have all the creature comforts of a good hotel including furnished bedrooms, modern toilets, cozy living rooms, a kitchen and even a balcony for angling. itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.title: Wednesday - New Delhi
paragraphs:
The journey of a lifetime begins at the Delhi Safdarjung Railway station where the guests are accorded a warm, traditional welcome before the Palace-on-Wheels pulls out into the night for a week-long luxury cruise through fascinating Rajasthan.

Reporting Time 18.00 Dep. 18.30

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.title: Thursday, Arrival 3.45 Departure 11.30
paragraphs: Jaipur: Your tour began at the Hawa Mahal Palace of wind followed the amazing Jantar Mantar-Astronomical Observatory are to be explored at leisure.

The home of the erstwhile rulers. The city palace now a museum of full royal splendor. Jaipur also offers a great shopping experience since the city is the countries capital as far as handicrafts are concerned.

This include a very extensive range as well as a major International center of cutting and polishing of Gems and stone. Also the Jaipur is known all over the world for hand block printing on textile. Lunch at Amber Fort. Soon after reaching at Amber you can enjoy the festively decorated elephant for a ride up to the fort.
After lunch visit of Amber fort the best example of splendid fusion of Rajput and Mugal style of Architecture.
The hall of victory Jai Mandir has a stunning ceiling adorned with mirror work an inlaid panel. Return back to train by bus for fresh n up after rest awhile enjoy sumptuous dinner on board.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.title: Friday, Swai Madhopur Arrival 5.30 Departure 10.30
paragraphs: Sawai Madhopur The Ranthambhore national park at junction of the Aravali and the Vindhyas is a unique juxtaposition of natural and historical richness, standing out conspicuously in the vast, arid and denuded tract of eastern Rajasthan, barely 14 Kms from Sawai Madhopur.

A 1000 year old Ranthambhore Fort of great historical importance atop a high hill stand tall remain of the historical part cenotaphs, tombs, stepped well, summer palace etc, have all merged harmoniously in to the sprawling forest.

Three big lakes- Padam Talav, Malik Talav and Raj bag- are alike turquoises studded in the vast tract. Though a delicate eco system, Ranthambhore is dynamic in the diversity and density of fauna it supports.Tiger at the apex of the food chain lords over the kingdom in a subtle way solitary by nature. It operates with stealth. Quite naturally tiger sighting are always a matter of chance, though evidences of its activities are equally exciting other then tigers you may have opportunity to see 24 different species of mammals, spotted deer, sambhar, wild boar, Indian Gazel, Jungal cat, Panthers, Jackal, Hynas Rarely sloth bears, also almost 300 different kind of birds.
Return back to Palace on Wheels. Break fast on Board.
Lunch on Board.
Enjoy the afternoon on train as it travels the lush green country side before arriving to Chittorgarh.

Chittorgarh Fort is considered as the largest fort of India, built by various Mauriyan rulers during 5th to 8th century period, this for covers an area of 680 acres most of the structures in side the fort premises are in ruins. But a glimpses at this giant abodes of Rajput still fills on with thrill. The fort is accessible after ceremony seven gates. Rana Kumbha palace and Padamini Palace in the fort are considered as master pieces of Rajput architecture Padmini Palace had been the residence of beautiful queen Rani Padmini.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.title: Saturday, Udaipur Arrival 8.00 Departure 3.30
paragraphs: The capital of the Sisodia Maharanas, enjoy pre-eminen among the Rajput clams of Rajasthan spend the day sight seeing at Udaipur Maharana Udai Singh, Laid the foundation for a new kingdom Udaipur situated at Lake Pichola where the impressive city palace was lavished with aesthetic and imaginative work of art miniature painting was encouraged.
Subsequently the princes built the seemingly floating Irland Palace, the royal summer retreat, offering a spectacular view of the lake and surrounding mountains.
New Arrangement for this Season.
1. Break Fast on board.
2. Lunch at Palace Hotel
3. Visit to Crystal Gallery-It is a balcony of Fateh Prakash Banquet hall which is having a museum of crystal glass furniture, crockery, chandilliers of old time.
4. Boat Ride and back to train.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.title: Sunday, Jaisalmer Arrival 9.15 Departure 11.45
paragraphs: Jaisalmer The golden city of Rajasthan has a charm of its own, Rawal Jaisal a Bhati Rajput ruler founded the city in 1156 AD. The western most citadel of the desert, Jaisalmer has an ancient history linked with its development as a trading center. Located en-route one of the two passages, that connected India with persia, egypt Africa and West. The Bhati Rajput sole guardians of the city accumulate enough wealth through tax levied on the passing carwans. Jaisalmer amid picturesque a marvel of beautiful culture and harsh climate conditions. The Sonar Quila Fort, made of yellow sand stone will immediately command your attention here.

The city is also known for its old mansion better known as havelies. Patwon Ki Haveli and Nathmalgi Ke Haveli, Salim Singh Ji Ki Haveli most striking architecture a fine blend of ancient and the medieval era. Shopping and lunch at Moomal Hotel. The sweeping sand dunes, enjoy the romance of solitude at Kuldhara and your camel takes you deep in the thar desert, the set hare is the most awaited experience. As the sum sets the rolling golden dunes the surreal experience is worth. Though the winter, followed by the cultural performance – campfire with dinner in dunes.
New Arrangements for this Season.
1. Enjoy Rajasthani Food with traditional music.
2. Evening Tea, Sun set.
3. Dinner at Palace Hotel.

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.title: Monday, Jodhpur Arrival 7.00 Departure 3.30
paragraphs: Special welcome on arrival and sightseeing of mighty fort followed by lunch at Star hotel.

The city best known for its indigo-hued homes and buildings, Jodhpur is the former capital of the Marwar. The Mehrangarh Fort was built by Rao Jodha in 1459 and later his successions also added new structures. The fort is situated 120 meters high rocky hill, this fort is witness the lavish and royal history of Rathore.
Fort stands on strong and wide walls, which are 20 to 120 feet high and 12 to 70 feet thick its gigantic structure and finely carved intricate sculpture are a treat for eye.

The royal structure boast their own saga of security and beauty the perl palace has a delicately carved stone screen, umaid vilas displays the Rajput miniature paintings and the ajit vilas exhibits musical instruments and the royal costumes. Shopping of local handicrafts.

Umaid Bhawan Palace worlds finest and largest palace in the world Maharaja Umaid Singh utilized the services of a well known Edwardian architect, henry vaughan lanchester for the construction of this palace. There are 347 rooms in the palace that boast about its grandness and splendor the central dome that has become the identity of the palace 110 feet high. The royal family in still lives a part of the palace also having the old clock museum.
Lunch at 5 Star Hotel. After lunch back to Palace on Wheels, dinner on board.

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.title: Tuesday, Bharatpur Arrival 5.00 Departure 8.45
paragraphs: Bharatpur A royal kingdom where the jats, rather than the Rajputs, ruled. Bharatpur’s Jat History is not too old, with Suraj Mal establishing a firm stronghold in a region contested by both the Rajputs and the Mughals. Suraj Mal exploits are legendary, and the fort, Lohargarh, or Iron Fort, has a history that recounts it with pride. The only fort in the state to have bastions of mud, these proved meritorious because they simply swallowed up the cannon shells not allowing them to impact.

The Keoladeo Ghana National Park one of the finest bird sanctuary in the world was developed by a royal edict when dykes were created so that water could be canalized for the hunting preserve as the Maharaja of Bharatpur wished to create.
Over three hundred species of birds many of them migrant species that come from parts as distant as Siberia and China.
New Arrangement for This season:
1. Break Fast on board.

Agra A visit to the world’s most well known monument and well worth its fame. The Taj Mahal built in the memory of his beloved empress by emperor Shah Jahan, this marble mausoleum is the greatest gesture of love known to mankind and is breathtakingly, bewitchingly beautiful. Land for the building of the Taj Mahal in Agra came fromthe Maharaja of Jaipur and the marble used in its construction was from the mines of Makrana, also in Rajasthan. The precious stones used in its inlay, and the craftsmen employed for the twenty two years its construction took, came not only from India, but from all over the World.
New Arrangement for this season.
1. Lunch at Palace Hotel.

intro:
Our Majestic South India Tour is the best tourist circuits in India to explore South India. This tourist circuits includes important locations which can explain itself their culture and diversity of different eras of this states. South India is well known for its brightly decorated temples with the Dravidian style of architecture, cultural monuments and mouth-watering dishes. Many of the temples are hundreds and thousands of years old.

In this land of temple spires, the devout and the connoisseur of art both pay homage. Highlights of South India include the Brahadehswara Temple at Thanjavur. Magnificent shadow of its 81.3 ton monolithic cupola never falls on the ground. The Meenakshi temple at Madurai dedicated to the fish-eyed goddess. The Nizam’s splendours of Hyderabad; the garden city of Bangalore; sandalwood-scented Mysore.

For the art-inclined, there is the stylised elegance of Bharata Natyam, the story-telling art of Kathakali and the martial-art grace of Kalaripayattu.
